We can see that this data contains 120 features. To predict the ranking of the next premier league's season I will not use all of these features. We fist start by combining all of the different datasets into one large one. Since all of the observations are recorded in cronological order it is easy to understand why we will just merge the observations following a cronological order.

We won't use all of the features of this data so now we want to clean the data.

To do:
1.check which dataset has the maximum number of columns
2.merge the datasets wrt the number of columns in this maxcoldataset (i.e. it'll appear NA for all the observations without that feature recorded)


```{r}

vectordata<-list(fixtures26_27=fixtures26_27, data26_27 = data26_27, data25_26 = data25_26, data24_25 = data24_25, data23_24 = data23_24, data22_23 = data22_23, data21_22 = data21_22, data20_21 = data20_21, data19_20 = data19_20, data18_19 = data18_19, data17_18 = data17_18, data16_17 = data16_17, data15_16 = data15_16, data14_15 = data14_15)

columncheck <- function(a) {
  coln <- sapply(a, ncol) #applies the function ncol() to each dataset
  names(coln)[which.max(coln)]
}

print(columncheck(vectordata))

```
Now we know that the latest observations are the ones containing the larger number of features.
```{r}
ncol(data25_26)
```
Hence we now merge the datasets wrt the columns of the `data25_26` dataset.
```{r}
matches<-c()
for (i in seq_along(vectordata)) {
  matches[i] <-sum(colnames(data25_26) %in% colnames(vectordata[[i]]))
}
names(matches) <- names(vectordata)
print(matches) 
```
Here we now know that `data18_19` has the least number of feature matches wrt `data25_26`. We want to check which columns of these datasets are different to the ones of `data25_26`.
```{r}
colnames(data18_19)[which(!colnames(data18_19) %in% colnames(data25_26))]
```
IWH = Interwetten home win odds
IWD = Interwetten draw odds
IWA = Interwetten away win odds
VCH = VC Bet home win odds (now BetVictor)
VCD = VC Bet draw odds (now BetVictor)
VCA = VC Bet away win odds (now BetVictor)
Bb1X2 = Number of BetBrain bookmakers used to calculate match odds averages and maximums
BbMxH = Betbrain maximum home win odds
BbAvH = Betbrain average home win odds
BbMxD = Betbrain maximum draw odds
BbAvD = Betbrain average draw win odds
BbMxA = Betbrain maximum away win odds
BbAvA = Betbrain average away win odds
BbOU = Number of BetBrain bookmakers used to calculate over/under 2.5 goals (total goals) averages and maximums
BbMx>2.5 = Betbrain maximum over 2.5 goals
BbAv>2.5 = Betbrain average over 2.5 goals
BbMx<2.5 = Betbrain maximum under 2.5 goals
BbAv<2.5 = Betbrain average under 2.5 goals
BbAH = Number of BetBrain bookmakers used to Asian handicap averages and maximums
BbAHh = Betbrain size of handicap (home team)
BbMxAHH = Betbrain maximum Asian handicap home team odds
BbAvAHH = Betbrain average Asian handicap home team odds
BbMxAHA = Betbrain maximum Asian handicap away team odds
BbAvAHA = Betbrain average Asian handicap away team odds

Notice that all of these variables represent the odds of a match. Since these features depend on people's perception, I will not be using these in my model as I only want to train my model on match statistics.

To clean the data I will now just delete all the odds columns from all of the datasets and only keep match statistics.

```{r}
# columns to keep i.e. match information, results and match statistics
columns_to_keep <- c("Date", "HomeTeam", "AwayTeam","FTHG", "HG", "FTAG", "AG", "FTR", "Res","HTHG", "HTAG", "HTR","Attendance","Referee", "HS", "AS", "HST", "AST", "HHW", "AHW","HC", "AC", "HF", "AF", "HFKC", "AFKC","HO", "AO", "HY", "AY", "HR", "AR", "HBP", "ABP")


for (i in seq_along(vectordata)) {
  columns_removed <- setdiff(names(vectordata[[i]]), columns_to_keep) #odds columns

  vectordata[[i]] <- vectordata[[i]][, intersect(columns_to_keep, names(vectordata[[i]])),drop = FALSE]
}

```
As we can see, the older (or incomplete for `data26_27`) the dataset is, the less features it contains. This will then be spoken about in the limitations section of our report. This means that we want the model to be weighted more strongly for the newer datasets.

## Test/Train split

Firstly we define out test/train split.
```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(stats)
library(base)

train_data <- bind_rows(vectordata[train_names])
test_data  <- bind_rows(vectordata["data25_26"])
```

We keep 2026/27 separate as the data we'll predict from.

```{r}
prediction_data <- bind_rows(vectordata["data26_27"])
fixtures26_27 <- bind_rows(vectordata["fixtures26_27"])
prediction_data <- bind_rows(prediction_data, fixtures26_27) 
```

Now `prediction_data` contains all fixtures of 2026/27 season and `NA` for starts of matches that haven't been played.
Now we want to add extra columns to simplify our model calculations. First we consider the whole dataset as one and split it wrt seasons.

```{r}

all_data <- rbind(train_data, test_data, prediction_data)
#split observations by season
all_data$Date <- as.Date(as.character(all_data$Date), format = "%d/%m/%Y") #treat `Date` as date format 
match_year <- as.integer(format(all_data$Date, "%Y"))
match_month <- as.integer(format(all_data$Date, "%m"))

all_data$Season <- ifelse(match_month >= 7,match_year,match_year - 1) # adding a new column which represents the season

seasons <- unique(all_data$Season) # length = 13 
teams <- unique(c(all_data$HomeTeam, all_data$AwayTeam))#columns of all teams from 2014-2027 of length = 36

```

Since we want our model to use the previous match results to predict the next match result, we need to add a counting column which adds up the previous statistics up to until the previous match so that we can use this statistic for our prediction. This gives greater weight to more recent observations.

```{r}
#create a list of match statistics from earlier matches to keep track
stats <- list(FTGoals= c("FTHG", "FTAG"), HTGoals = c("HTHG", "HTAG"), Shots = c("HS", "AS"), ShotsOnTarget = c("HST", "AST"), Corners = c("HC", "AC"), Fouls = c("HF", "AF"), YellowCards = c("HY", "AY"), RedCards = c("HR", "AR"))

all_data$.match_id <- seq_len(nrow(all_data)) #starts empty columns

for (stat in names(stats)) {
  home_stat <- stats[[stat]][1] #identifies all of the home stats columns
  away_stat <- stats[[stat]][2] #identifies all of the away stats columns
#creates new counting columns for each stat
  all_data[[paste0("Home", stat, "Before")]] <- 0
  all_data[[paste0("Away", stat, "Before")]] <- 0  

  for (season in unique(all_data$Season)) {
    for (team in teams) {
      rows <- which(all_data$Season == season & (all_data$HomeTeam == team | all_data$AwayTeam == team)) # look at the rows where this team has played

      team_stats <- ifelse(all_data$HomeTeam[rows] == team, all_data[[home_stat]][rows], all_data[[away_stat]][rows]) # if team is home, then we look at home_stat, o/w we look at away_stat
      team_stats[is.na(team_stats)] <- 0
      
      stat_before <- c(0, head(cumsum(team_stats), -1)) #summing up all of the stats up to previous match
      
        home_rows <- rows[all_data$HomeTeam[rows] == team] #identify the rows in which our team is home team
        away_rows <- rows[all_data$AwayTeam[rows] == team] #identify the rows in which our team is away team

        all_data[[paste0("Home", stat, "Before")]][home_rows] <- stat_before[all_data$HomeTeam[rows] == team] #add to home stat column when team is home

        all_data[[paste0("Away", stat, "Before")]][away_rows] <- stat_before[all_data$AwayTeam[rows] == team] #add away stat column when team is away
      
    }
  }
}

all_data$.match_id <- NULL


```

Now we also want to add the following columns to our model:
- Home Team total points before match = HTPB
- Home team total points after match = HTPA
- Away Team total points before match = ATPB
- Away team total points after match = ATPA
Adds columns that keeps track of the points. We do this separately since the number of points depends on a different condition.

```{r}
# Create the new columns
all_data$HTPB <- NA
all_data$HTPA <- NA
all_data$ATPB <- NA
all_data$ATPA <- NA

for(season in seasons){
  for (team in teams) {
  
    #find every match involving this team in this season
    rows <- which(all_data$Season == season & (all_data$HomeTeam == team | all_data$AwayTeam == team))
  
    # Points this team earned in each match
    points <- ifelse(all_data$HomeTeam[rows] == team, ifelse(all_data$FTR[rows] == "H", #if team is home and FTR = H then 3,
                                                             3,
                                                             ifelse(all_data$FTR[rows] == "D", # if FTR = D then 1 o/w 0
                                                                    1,
                                                                    0)),
                                                      ifelse(all_data$FTR[rows] == "A", #if team is not home and FTR = A then 3,
                                                             3,
                                                             ifelse(all_data$FTR[rows] == "D", # if FTR = D then 1 o/w 0
                                                                    1,
                                                                    0))
                     )
    points[is.na(points)] <- 0
  
    # Running total before and after each match
    points_before <- c(0, head(cumsum(points), -1))
    points_after  <- cumsum(points)
  
    # Store the totals in the home or away columns
    home_rows <- rows[all_data$HomeTeam[rows] == team]
    away_rows <- rows[all_data$AwayTeam[rows] == team]
  
    all_data$HTPB[home_rows] <- points_before[all_data$HomeTeam[rows] == team]
    all_data$HTPA[home_rows] <- points_after[all_data$HomeTeam[rows] == team]
    all_data$ATPB[away_rows] <- points_before[all_data$AwayTeam[rows] == team]
    all_data$ATPA[away_rows] <- points_after[all_data$AwayTeam[rows] == team]
  }
}

#split the datasets apart
train_data <- all_data[1:nrow(train_data), ]

test_start <- nrow(train_data) + 1
test_end <- nrow(train_data) + nrow(test_data)
test_data <- all_data[test_start:test_end, ]

prediction_start <- test_end + 1
prediction_data <- all_data[prediction_start:nrow(all_data), ]
```
